target.title: security(audit): flag control-plane exposure and plugin command surfaces
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two related gaps in `openclaw security audit` where operators could miss high-impact exposure on open chat surfaces and extension plugin command entry points.

### Gap 1: Control-plane tools on open inbound policy

When a channel uses `groupPolicy="open"` or an open DM policy, prompt injection in those conversations can drive agent tool calls. The exposure matrix already flagged:

- elevated tools (`security.exposure.open_groups_with_elevated`)
- runtime/filesystem tools without sandbox or workspace guards (`security.exposure.open_groups_with_runtime_or_fs`)

It did **not** separately flag **control-plane tools** (`cron`, `gateway`) that can reconfigure the gateway or manipulate scheduled runs. A common example: `tools.profile="coding"` on an open WhatsApp group allows `cron` while runtime/fs may be sandboxed — the audit could report a clean runtime/fs posture while `cron` remained reachable from untrusted chat input.

### Gap 2: Extension plugin commands on chat command surfaces

The plugin trust audit warned when extensions existed without `plugins.allow`, but severity escalation depended only on **native skill commands** being enabled. It did not:

- evaluate **native command** surfaces separately from native skill commands
- name which configured channels expose command surfaces in the finding detail
- warn when **enabled extension plugins register commands** that may be reachable on those surfaces

Plugin commands bypass the LLM and run before built-in commands and agent invocation. Operators with Discord (or other channels) auto-enabling native commands and unallowlisted extensions could receive only a generic warn-level finding without understanding the bypass risk.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Control-plane exposure (sync audit)

`collectRiskyToolExposureContexts()` in `src/security/audit-extra.sync.ts` now probes `cron` and `gateway` alongside existing runtime/fs checks. Control-plane exposure is tracked in a separate `riskyControlPlaneContexts` list because sandbox mode does not mitigate gateway/cron control the way it mitigates exec/filesystem tools.

When open inbound policy is present and any agent context allows control-plane tools, the audit emits a new finding:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `checkId` | `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` |
| `severity` | `critical` |
| `remediation` | Deny `group:automation` (or explicitly deny `cron`/`gateway`) for exposed agents; keep control-plane tools limited to trusted operator sessions |

The multi-user heuristic (`security.trust_model.multi_user_heuristic`) now includes control-plane context lines when present, and its impact summary distinguishes control-plane exposure from runtime/process exposure.

### Plugin command surface audit (async plugin trust)

`collectPluginsTrustFindings()` in `src/security/audit-plugins-trust.ts` adds `collectConfiguredCommandSurfaces()`, which resolves per-channel:

- **native commands** via `resolveNativeCommandsEnabled()` (respecting channel overrides, global `commands.native`, and plugin `nativeCommandsAutoEnabled`)
- **native skill commands** via `resolveNativeSkillsEnabled()` (existing behavior, now shared helper)

Changes to existing and new findings:

| `checkId` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` | `warn`; critical only when native **skill** commands enabled | `critical` when **native commands or native skill commands** enabled on any configured channel; detail names affected surfaces |
| `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` | *(did not exist)* | `warn` when enabled extension plugins register commands **and** native commands are enabled on configured surfaces |

The plugin registry snapshot is loaded once per audit pass and reused for phantom allowlist checks and command registration lookup. Command reachability is intentionally gated on **native commands** (not native skills alone) because plugin-registered commands route through the native command surface.

## User Impact

- **Operators** running `openclaw security audit` get clearer, actionable findings when open chats can reach gateway/cron control or extension plugin commands.
- **Severity changes**: `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` may now report `critical` on setups that previously showed `warn` when native commands (not just native skills) are active without `plugins.allow`.
- **No runtime behavior change**: gateway, tool policy, plugin loading, and command dispatch are unchanged. This is audit output only.

## Evidence

### Focused tests

```bash
pnpm test src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts
```

Result (local, macOS):

```text
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
   Duration  ~3s
```

### Trust-model test matrix (`audit-trust-model.test.ts`)

| Scenario | Expected finding | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open WhatsApp group + `tools.profile="coding"` | `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` | critical |
| Same + `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode="all"` | No `open_groups_with_runtime_or_fs`; no `open_groups_with_control_plane` when automation denied by policy interaction | — |
| Open group + `deny: ["group:automation"]` | No `open_groups_with_control_plane` | — |
| Discord allowlist + multi-user heuristic signals + runtime/automation denied | `security.trust_model.multi_user_heuristic` detail includes `No exposed control-plane contexts detected.` | warn |

### Plugin trust test matrix (`audit-plugins-trust.test.ts`)

| Scenario | Expected finding | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Extensions present, no `plugins.allow`, no configured channels | `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` | warn |
| Extensions + configured Discord (native commands auto-enabled) + no `plugins.allow` | `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` with `Native commands are enabled` in detail | critical |
| `plugins.allow=["some-plugin"]` + Discord + plugin registers commands | `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` + `plugins.tools_reachable_permissive_policy` | warn |
| Same + `tools.profile="coding"` | Command reachability warn; permissive tool policy **not** flagged | — |
| Same + `commands.native=false` | No `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` | — |
| Discord token via SecretRef env ref | Still critical `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` with bypass explanation | critical |

## Before / after behavior examples

### Example A: Open group with coding profile

**Config sketch:**

```json
{
  "channels": { "whatsapp": { "groupPolicy": "open" } },
  "tools": { "elevated": { "enabled": false }, "profile": "coding" }
}
```

**Before:** May flag runtime/fs exposure; `cron` allowed by coding profile not called out as control-plane risk.

**After:** Emits `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` naming contexts where `cron` (and `gateway` if allowed) are reachable.

### Example B: Discord + extensions, no allowlist

**Config sketch:**

```json
{
  "channels": { "discord": { "enabled": true, "token": "..." } }
}
```

(with extension directories present under state)

**Before:** `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` at `warn` unless native **skills** explicitly enabled.

**After:** `critical` because Discord native commands auto-enable on configured surfaces; detail lists `discord` and explains plugin commands bypass the LLM.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/security/audit-extra.sync.ts` | Control-plane probe; new exposure finding; multi-user heuristic detail |
| `src/security/audit-plugins-trust.ts` | `collectConfiguredCommandSurfaces()`; severity/detail updates; new command reachability finding |
| `src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts` | Control-plane and deny-path regression cases |
| `src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts` | Native command surface mocks and command reachability cases |

## Non-goals and boundaries

- Does not change tool allow/deny enforcement at runtime.
- Does not add new config keys or env vars.
- Does not scan plugin command handlers for code safety (existing `--deep` plugin code scan remains separate).
- `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` is heuristic: it reports registry-registered commands on enabled extensions when native command surfaces are configured; it does not live-probe channel APIs.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

- Update [audit checks reference](/gateway/security/audit-checks) with `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane`, `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface`, and the revised severity for `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist`.

## Risk checklist

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| User-visible behavior change? | Yes — audit findings and severities may change for affected configs |
| Config / migration change? | No |
| Security / auth / network / tool execution change? | No at runtime; audit detection only |
| Highest-risk area | Operators who relied on warn-level `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` while native commands were active |
| Mitigation | Findings include explicit remediation text; no automatic enforcement |

## Current review state

- Next action: awaiting maintainer review
- Bot comments addressed: none yet

## AI-assisted disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- [x] Human-directed scope and review of audit logic
- [ ] `codex review --base origin/main` (not run yet)
